arch/x86/kvm/pkvm/Makefile.rationale: This path implements the Intel pKVM protected-host backend, not ordinary upstream KVM. In pinned ACK arch/x86/kvm/pkvm.c, enable_pkvm is a zero-initialized bool; vmx/pkvm_init.c sets it only via early kvm-intel.pkvm parsing and exits before hypervisor setup when false. The supplied goldfish board/kernel/x86_64.mk explicitly installs x86_64_cmdline.txt, whose complete contents are 8250.nr_uarts=1 clocksource=pit. This current SDK boot contract does not request the protected-host mode. Omit this backend for the current target and retain exact LTS state. Ordinary Intel/AMD KVM stays enabled. This does not assert that all AVF userspace is absent, that nested virtualization cannot exist, or that future protected-VM requirements are resolved; the decision is limited to the supplied ordinary SDK boot configuration.

kernel/module/Kconfig.rationale: Read complete added options. kernel/module/internal.h.rationale: Read full export/lookup metadata delta and companion producer/consumer. Unified symbol/CRC/flag tables preserve GPL semantics. f08e12b0ed1a declares the protected-export array with its actual PREL32 s32 type (or pointer entries for the absolute format), matching PROTECT_EXPORT assembly; pointer-width indexing previously skipped 330 of 659 names in the x86 SDK artifact. Native module/load state retained. This is regenerated metadata, not old binary layout preservation.

kernel/module/main.c.rationale: Read complete LTS-to-port and normalized-ACK-to-port deltas, load order, section helpers and native signature verifier. Retain Android SCM identity, unified symbol/flag lookup, signed export protection and three trusted vendor memory/permission hooks. Keep LTS CAP_SYS_MODULE/modules_disabled, signature/lockdown, module reference, duplicate/GPL export, ELF SHT_STRTAB validation, codetag error propagation/livepatch cleanup and unsigned-module taint checks. Hooks run around native lifecycle and after successful native ROX/ro-after-init protection; a trusted callback can deliberately alter permission policy. f08e12b0ed1a fixes PREL32 table stride, absolute-pointer dereference, and rejects flags sections whose byte count differs from the symbol count before lookup. Build-34 ELF audit verifies 145 flag/CRC tables and demonstrates the old search misses 330/659 protected names; the 4-byte search finds all. This is metadata evidence, not runtime module-loading enforcement. No historical whitelist restrictions or unsigned-taint suppression retained.

drivers/dma-buf/dma-buf.c.rationale: Full LTS and normalized-ACK residuals reviewed. Retain accounting for per-process DMA-buf RSS/PSS and high-water marks: pinned GrapheneOS lmkd.cpp reads dmabuf_pss for victim sizing, and libmeminfo has procfs API tests (read, not executed). State uses refcounts and locks, counts actual child FDs/VMAs, shares only when both MM/files are shared, and intentionally leaves partial sharing/kernel threads unaccounted. Preallocation avoids sleeping under the accounting spinlock; 54fdb0c6e4bd trims unused records after fork and failed preallocation so duplicate FDs/VMAs cannot leave an unbounded per-CPU cache. Keep Android buffer iteration, naming, partial CPU-access and flags APIs plus release hook; 90d9af708fea guards NULL partial-end access and supplies zero default flags. Native LTS mapping bounds, reservation/fence waits, poll, sync-file ioctls and release behavior remain. Accounting failures on mmap log and preserve successful mapping; fork/exec allocations can fail with ENOMEM. Cross-file VMA/fd/fork lifecycle paths retain separate candidate reviews. No runtime correctness or OOM-policy test claim. Incremental review a7db20b7e4ce: count duplicate references without allocation; after a missing new record, keep tracking/draining existing records but prohibit new records and return EIO from RSS/PSS/HWM interfaces. This avoids an untracked close subtracting a later unrelated attribution. Details and compatibility/security limitations are in evidence/dmabuf-accounting-local-review.json and SECURITY.md. No native LTS I/O, fence or file lifetime path is replaced.

drivers/dma-buf/dma-heap.c.rationale: Full LTS/normalized-ACK delta and native cdev/device lifetime machinery reviewed. Retain source find/put/alloc/get-device APIs and allocation hooks for Android heap customization. Preserve native LTS fd reservation, result copy and only then installation, with cleanup on copy failure; never call the early-install helper from ioctl. 5694a9ef32df makes open files hold heap references, serializes publication/error cleanup/open/find/final removal, separates cdev kobject allocation from heap storage to survive racing opens, and balances the extra device reference. Acquire-load allocation callback pairs with system heap release publication. Exporters still own callback/module lifetime; no arbitrary module unload guarantee is introduced. Existing flag validation and real-page allocation alignment remain. Compilation verification is separate from runtime allocation/race testing. eecae28e83be corrects the callback local declaration after build 36 showed that typeof inherited const from the operations table; acquire/release semantics remain. Build 37 passed common kernel compilation; build 38 completed the full workflow after declaring the external heap cleanup import, with all 145 signatures verified. No runtime allocation/race test.

drivers/dma-buf/heaps/Kconfig.rationale: Full change permits system and CMA heap drivers as tristates. The actual manifest virtual-device fragment enables DMABUF_HEAPS_SYSTEM=m and BUILD.bazel distributes system_heap.ko, even though the common kernel config has it unset. drivers/dma-buf/heaps/cma_heap.c.rationale: Full residual forwards caller DMA mapping attributes symmetrically on map/unmap and supplies module license/namespace imports needed by tristate source builds. drivers/dma-buf/heaps/system_heap.c.rationale: Full LTS delta reviewed. Preserve cached and system-uncached heaps: pinned GrapheneOS BufferAllocator::AllocSystem selects the latter for no-CPU-access requests and explicitly falls back to system when absent; actual virtual-device rules build this module. Keep write-combined user/kernel mappings, zeroed pages, matching DMA attributes, and refuse uncached SWIOTLB mappings that cannot maintain the intended coherence contract. df0acacabb95 checks every SG entry instead of repeatedly checking the first, propagates initial map failure and releases the exported buffer without invalid unmap, validates DMA setup and release-publishes the allocator. If optional uncached registration fails after cached publication, retain cached service and successful module initialization so callbacks cannot point into freed failed-init module text. Mask-setup failure drops the uncached registration reference; existing open references may delay disappearance and see EBUSY. On x86 PAGE_SHIFT=12 allocation orders remain the LTS 8/4/0 values. No runtime allocation, cache-coherence, IOMMU/SWIOTLB or fault-injection validation.

include/linux/dma-buf.h.rationale: Full LTS and normalized-ACK deltas reviewed. The native LTS fd publication helper is represented by a local fd_install wrapper because this selected tree has no fd tracepoint; ioctl still installs only after copy succeeds. Disabled-config stubs leave native paths unchanged. Partial access remains a trusted kernel/exporter contract, with range/coherence obligations at callers and callbacks; it is not a new userspace partial-access ioctl. Incremental review a7db20b7e4ce: count duplicate references without allocation; after a missing new record, keep tracking/draining existing records but prohibit new records and return EIO from RSS/PSS/HWM interfaces. fs/file.c.rationale: Reviewed all LTS and normalized-ACK differences and complete do_dup2/close/fd-install paths with DMA accounting implementation. Retain accounting before fd publication, unaccount before last file release, files_struct ownership, and removal of task accounting on partial sharing. do_dup2 holds a file reference while dropping file_lock for preallocation; on relock it re-reads the table and preserves native reserved-slot EBUSY/nospec checks. Rollback unaccounts and drops the added file reference; replaced files are unaccounted before close. Allocation failure in fd_install is best effort: it logs and installs the descriptor, so counters can undercount under OOM and are not resource limits. Retain GPL file_close_fd export and Android close_fd source namespace. Remaining file equals normalized ACK; no historical KMI layout retained. Positive lmkd dmabuf PSS/RSS and libmeminfo proc consumers are documented in SECURITY.md.

After successful copy_dmabuf_info, later failures release the task reference, then MM/files teardown drops their separate references; delayed_free_task calls free_task, not __put_task_struct, so no second task-info put. Keep cpufreq time allocation/init/free, actual vendor/OEM runtime data initialization, task/MM hooks and source exports. Proxy scheduling fields/locks/lists are initialized for the retained implementation; its scheduling algorithms are assessed separately. Integrity-hook failure uses bad_fork_core_free, preserving both locks and scheduler cleanup. Preserve native LTS early BPF initialization, CLONE_VM futex-hash sharing including vfork, PF_BLOCK_TS clearing and namespace API. Accounting OOM can fail fork; no runtime fork/race certification.

Native LTS get_pid/put_pid keeps thread_pid alive across proc_flush_pid, native pending-signal teardown avoids double flush, and sched_mm_cid_exit and exit_nsproxy_namespaces remain. Hooks do not bypass native exit cleanup. No runtime task-exit test.

Policy tables persist and reuse existing CPU entries; dynamic driver replacement and runtime concurrency are not verified.

drivers/cpufreq/cpufreq.c.rationale: Reviewed complete LTS/normalized-ACK deltas. Hook callbacks can override requested frequency policy and remain trusted module code. 71542ccb67ed restores native LTS max_freq_req reactivation update: ACK fe0fb52b0590 calls it redundant after generic boost synchronization, but this cleanup provides no required Android behavior. kernel/sched/cputime.c.rationale: Full net delta retains cpufreq task-time accounting on user/system CPU time, GPL CPU IRQ-time/thread-group-time exports and Android accounting callbacks.
